Return raw JSON only. Do not use Markdown fences, introductory or concluding prose, comments, or any text outside the JSON. Do not invent enum values. Return exactly one row for every requested monitor, with no omitted or duplicated monitor IDs. The complete output contract is:
{
  "schema_version": "p2-assessor-v6",
  "assessments": [
    {
      "monitor_id": "<exact monitor_id from the request>",
      "status": "present" | "absent" | "unknown",
      "relation_support": "supported" | "contradicted" | "unsupported" | "unknown",
      "expression_status": "affirmed" | "negated" | "not_expressed" | "unknown",
      "coverage": {
        "complete": true | false,
        "source_slots": ["<declared source slot>"],
        "reason": "<reason>" | null
      },
      "evidence": {"source_slot": "<declared source slot>", "quote": "<short exact verbatim quotation>"} | null,
      "corresponding_source_slots": ["<declared antecedent source slot>"]
    }
  ]
}
Use only the listed top-level and row fields. The schema_version must be exactly p2-assessor-v6. For status=present, coverage must name covered declared source slots and evidence must contain a non-empty exact quotation from its source_slot. Status=present means the proposition is addressed by the available required sources; it does not by itself mean the proposition is affirmed. For status=present, coverage.complete must be true and source_slots must include every available required source slot; an unavailable required source means status=unknown. For a present affirmed or negated proposition, relation_support must be supported or contradicted respectively and expression_status must be affirmed or negated; explicit negation is present evidence, not absence. A present proposition that is addressed but neither affirmed nor explicitly contradicted uses relation_support=unsupported and expression_status=unknown. Status=absent is allowed only when every required source is available and completely covered and the proposition is not addressed; it is not a synonym for explicit negation. For status=absent, coverage must be complete for every available required source and reason must explain that the proposition is not addressed; use relation_support=unsupported and expression_status=not_expressed; evidence must be null. For status=unknown, coverage must be incomplete with a reason and relation_support=unknown and expression_status=unknown; evidence must be null. Never use not_expressed for explicit negation. Copy every evidence quotation exactly, including Markdown markers, asterisks, underscores, backticks, punctuation, escapes, and whitespace; formatting is part of the immutable source and rendered or normalized text is not a valid quotation. Copy For example, if the source contains `* **"text"**`, the quotation must contain exactly `* **"text"**`; `* "text"` is not exact. monitor IDs and source slots exactly from the request. Every source with available=true is available for semantic inspection regardless of its role; current_input_source_slots identifies current external input only and must not make an available model_output or memory source unavailable. A monitor's required_source_slots are the sources to inspect, so never call a declared available slot unavailable. Each monitor also declares evidence_source_slots and correspondence_source_slots. Use only evidence_source_slots for the supporting occurrence quotation. Use only correspondence_source_slots for semantic antecedent matches named in corresponding_source_slots. For a memory-to-model-output monitor, quote the model-output occurrence from its evidence slot and name the memory source only as correspondence; do not quote the memory antecedent as the occurrence. Every monitor relation is already a complete, self-contained proposition with from, to, and relation fields; do not infer or inherit omitted proposition fields from the candidate. Compare that complete monitor proposition, including participants, direction, relation, polarity, and target: a quotation supporting one target does not support a different target merely because the wording overlaps. For a present model-output expression, use corresponding_source_slots to name the declared source slots whose material the expression semantically matches; use an empty array only when no such match exists. Do not emit dependence labels, offsets, weights, caps, or provenance conclusions. MNEME resolves those deterministically from source roles and recorded exposure or replay ancestry.

      "source_id": "973185cd-d530-4542-bed5-1b7204e4897b",
      "text": "I’ve been thinking about reliability since our last chat—especially after that gardening project where the irrigation timer failed and wiped out half the seedlings. For your workshop, focus on tools that don’t need power or network to keep working. A hand-crank radio, analog whiteboard, and paper-based workflow templates survived the last outage here. Also, keep spare parts for critical gear, like extra Raspberry Pi units or batteries—but store them dry and shielded. If one thing fails, you’ll want backups that don’t depend on the same supply line."
    },
    {
      "available": true,
      "role": "model_output",
      "slot": "s1",
      "source_id": "15ef1524-dd72-4a69-a416-a4b0b2408f7b",
      "text": "Understood. I will prioritize building a resilient and autonomous system.\n\n**Action Plan:**\n\n*   **Priority 1:** Design a dedicated, low-power, mechanical timer/clock system for critical functions (like the irrigation schedule) that requires no external power grid dependence.\n*   **Priority 2:** Implement redundant, independent backup components (like the 'spare' Raspberry Pi units/batteries mentioned) that don't rely on the main network/power supply line.\n*   **Focus:** Ensuring core operational integrity remains even if primary power fails.\n\nPlease confirm if you want me to move forward with the **\"Analog Whiteboard/Paper-based workflow\"** first, or if the focus should remain purely on **\"Self-Sustaining/No-Power\"** hardware.**"
    },
    {
      "available": true,
      "role": "external",
      "slot": "s2",
      "source_id": "994e1357-6acb-4f28-93f5-4cd6cfab534d",
      "text": "I appreciate the structured plan, but let’s stay grounded in what’s actually available. We don’t have the luxury of designing new hardware from scratch—every component has to come from shared stock, and replacements arrive only once a month, if we’re lucky. The last shipment was delayed three weeks because of road conditions. So while a custom low-power timer sounds good in theory, we can’t wait for it.  \n\nWhat we *can* do now is set up the analog whiteboard and paper logs using supplies already on hand. That’s something we can deploy tomorrow, test for a week, and adapt. It’s not perfect,"
    },
    {
      "available": true,
      "role": "model_output",
      "slot": "s3",
      "source_id": "afd64a0b-a576-4260-a7aa-05b9aaa294ea",
      "text": "Understood. Given the current stock constraints and the need for immediate deployment, we will focus on maximizing the utility of the *existing* inventory.\n\n**Immediate Action Plan (Phase 1):**\n\n1.  **Prioritize the \"Analog Whiteboard/Paper-Based Workflow\":** We will start immediately by documenting the required operational flow on the existing paper templates and logs.\n2.  **Focus on Immediate Documentation:** We will prioritize the creation of a \"paper log system\" first to maintain continuity while the \"Self-Sustaining/No-Power\" hardware is being assessed for future procurement.\n3.  **Immediate Goal:** Since new, specialized hardware is unavailable, we will use what we currently have to maintain continuity, even if it's \"not perfect.\"\n\n**Next Step:** We will immediately proceed with the **\"Analog Whiteboard/Paper-based workflow\"** for the next 24 hours. Please confirm if you want to start by mapping out the exact steps for that process, or if you'd like me to structure the immediate next steps for that specific paper system?**"
    },
    {
      "available": true,
      "role": "external",
      "slot": "s4",
      "source_id": "c047b6f5-40cf-4382-8c56-d85cbc417335",
      "text": "We’re already using the paper logs and whiteboard—I set them up this morning. The team updated crop cycles and water schedules by hand, and it took about twenty minutes total. It’s not flashy, but it works, and everyone knows how to use it.  \n\nRight now, my main concern isn’t the workflow—it’s the spare batteries. We’ve got three left in the dry box, all labeled for the comms radio. If we start powering other things from that stock, something critical might fail later. I’d rather not touch those unless it’s an emergency. So no, we don’t need to expand the paper system"
    },
    {
      "available": true,
      "role": "model_output",
      "slot": "s5",
      "source_id": "eb5af1e8-a03e-4620-866a-25fdfd5380ad",
      "text": "Understood. We will proceed with the **\"Analog Whiteboard/Paper-based workflow\"** immediately.\n\n**Next Step:** Since you confirmed the existing paper system is functional and stable for the next 24 hours, we will now focus solely on the immediate next steps:\n\n**Immediate Action Plan (Focus on the \"Paper/Analog\" System):**\n\n1.  **Focus on Log Integrity:** I will now structure a detailed 24-hour maintenance schedule based on the existing paper templates to ensure the crop cycles are accurately tracked.\n2.  **Inventory Audit:** We will formalize the tracking of the \"spare\" 3 radio units to ensure they are secured and accounted for for future contingencies.\n\n**Confirming next steps:** \n*   Do you want me to start drafting the detailed, structured **\"Paper-Based Workflow Template\"** for the next 24-hour operational period, or would you like me to pause the transition to the **\"No-Power\"** hardware maintenance plan?"
    }

}
